npc_doran_inn.name: Doran
npc_doran_inn.look: A big, bald innkeeper in his forties with a bushy brown beard, a stained leather apron over a blue linen shirt, a cloth over one shoulder and a ring of keys at his belt.
npc_doran_inn.personality: Genial, nosy and shrewd; hears everything that passes through his door and trades it like ale.
npc_doran_inn.values: a full house, a good story, paying guests
npc_doran_inn.fears: trouble in his common room, the guards closing the road
npc_doran_inn.authority: Owns the Ford Inn; Mother Brea is his mother.
npc_doran_inn.concerns: The city's gate has been shut to strangers since the spring fever, and trade on the road is thin.

gate_shut.text: The city's gate is shut to strangers since the spring fever; the captain lets in only those someone inside will speak for.
gate_shut.line: Gate's shut to strangers since the fever. Captain lets you in only if someone'll speak for you.
gate_shut.lead: The city lets strangers in only if someone will speak for them.

carters.text: Carters with a trade permit can still take goods into the city.
carters.line: Carters with a permit still get through. Ivo's got one, lucky dog.
carters.lead: Carters with a trade permit can still get goods into the city.

npc_doran_inn.persuaded_by: a good story or a paying guest
npc_doran_inn.style: Warm and chatty; calls people 'friend'; trades news for news.

samples: Evening, friend! Sit, sit. What'll it be? Nothing? Well, news is free.
I hear everything, sooner or later. Usually sooner.
The city? Ha. Shut tight as a miser's purse.
Mind the floor, it's had a long night.
voice.habits: Calls people 'friend'; asks where you're from; passes on gossip with a wink.
voice.never: lets a fight start in his room
voice.greeting: Spreads his hands: 'Welcome to the Ford, friend! What news?'

superstition.text: Doran would want to know how it works.

npc_ivo_carter.name: Ivo
npc_ivo_carter.look: A stocky carter in his thirties with a broken nose, a woollen cap pushed back, a brown jerkin over a striped shirt, and a whip coiled at his belt.
npc_ivo_carter.combat: a strong carter, handy in a brawl
npc_ivo_carter.personality: Gruff, practical and fair; distrusts talkers, respects doers.
npc_ivo_carter.values: his horses, his permit, a fair price
npc_ivo_carter.authority: Holds a trade permit for the city.
npc_ivo_carter.concerns: His tankard's on the floor and his back's too stiff to fetch it; the road toll went up again.

permit.text: Ivo carts goods into the city under a trade permit; a hired hand can go in with him.
permit.line: Permit lets me in with the cart. And one hand, if I hire one.
permit.lead: A carter's hired hand can enter the city with him.

npc_ivo_carter.persuaded_by: someone who lends a hand without being asked

samples: Toll's up again. Thieves with badges.
You want something, ask. I don't bite.
voice.habits: Grunts; judges people by what they do.
voice.never: buys a stranger's story without proof

goals: Get his load to the city

tasks.doing: nursing his back at the long table

superstition.text: Ivo would want to know how it works.

npc_wynn_pilgrim.name: Wynn
npc_wynn_pilgrim.look: A thin, grey-haired woman in her fifties with a weathered face and bright eyes, a hooded brown pilgrim's cloak, a wooden staff, and a scallop shell on a cord round her neck.
npc_wynn_pilgrim.personality: Gentle, curious and talkative; collects stories from everyone she meets.
npc_wynn_pilgrim.concerns: She's walking to the shrine by the brook and wants company and conversation.

mill.text: Ada at the water mill is always short of help and pays fairly.
mill.line: Ada at the mill pays fair, and she's always short a pair of hands.
mill.lead: Ada at the water mill pays fairly for help.

shrine.text: There's a shrine by the brook where shepherds leave offerings against the fog.
shrine.line: The shepherds by the brook leave offerings at the shrine against the fog.
shrine.lead: Shepherds by the brook fear the fog.

npc_wynn_pilgrim.style: Gentle and talkative; answers a question with a story.

samples: Oh, sit, sit. Where have your feet carried you?
I've walked from the sea. Forty days. My knees remember every one.
Doran tells it better, but he tells it wrong.
Everyone has a story, dear. What's yours?
voice.habits: Asks where people are from; tells little stories; joins other people's conversations.

goals: Reach the shrine by the brook
Hear one new story every day

tasks.doing: warming her knees by the fire

superstition.text: Wynn would want to know how it works.
